text: Counsel for both the plaintiff and the defendant city filed briefs containing citations to non-existent cases. Plaintiff’s counsel admitted using “First Drafts”, an AI-powered legal drafting program, without verifying its output, and admitted using it in filings in other cases. Defence counsel admitted relying on a separate in-house AI research tool, which the order expressly calls “this unnamed software”, also without verification. Both resident attorneys let filings go out under their electronic signatures without review.
ai_system_name: "First Drafts" (named; admitted) and a second, expressly unnamed in-house legal-research tool
deployer: Kathleen M. Wilson (Wilson Law Firm LLC) and Kathryn Y. Williams (Daniel, Williams & Associates PLLC), with resident counsel Shauncey Hunter Ridgeway and Mark C. McClinton
canonical_source_conflicted: Citations to non-existent decisions, including a fabricated citation attributed to the same district; Fed. R. Civ. P. 11; Local Rule 83.1(c) and (d)(8)
mitigation_gap: Two independent AI research tools were used with no verification step, and the local-counsel review layer that exists precisely to catch this failed on both sides of the case simultaneously.
reliance_or_harm: Pro hac vice admission revoked for both lead attorneys, each additionally barred from entering an appearance in any case before the district for two years; both resident attorneys disqualified from further participation; fines totalling $8,000 payable to the court registry ($2,500, $3,500, $1,000, $1,000); AI-ethics CLE ordered for the attorney who had not previously attended one; the order transmitted to the Mississippi, Louisiana, and Texas bars, and to the judges presiding over two other matters involving the same counsel; all four attorneys terminated as counsel of record, leaving both litigants unrepresented under a deadline to obtain new counsel or face dismissal.
